input.quote: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: The only licence grant to us is Section 4(c) (p0021). It is helpfully perpetual, royalty-free and sublicensable, but "Company" is defined as Clear Capital alone (p0002), so the grant does not reach our affiliates and there is no path to add them by notice. Nor is the licence transferable: Section 10 (p0042) bars either party from assigning or transferring the Agreement or its rights without the other's prior written consent, so the licence would not follow us into a merger or acquisition. Both fallback elements therefore fail on material terms. We propose the shortest fallback cure: one sentence extending the licence to affiliates identified by written notice and permitting transfer to an M&A successor without Contractor's approval. We have not pressed the preferred elements (contractor coverage, express irrevocability) here.

ops.text: The foregoing license also extends to any affiliate of Company identified in a written notice to Contractor, and is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction without Contractor's approval.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the Section 4(c) licence to Company affiliates identified by written notice and made it transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition, which is our fallback licence-scope position; as drafted the licence runs to Clear Capital alone and Section 10 would block any transfer on a change of control.
proposal.summary: Extend the Section 4(c) licence to Company affiliates on written notice and make it transferable to an M&A successor.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
